title: Finite-rank extension of a square-zero-valued field derivation
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be fields of characteristic $p>0$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative $k$-algebra and $r:\Lambda\to K$ a ring map compatible with the $k$-structures. Let $I\subseteq\ker(r)$ be an ideal with $(\ker r)I=0$. Let $\sigma_0:K\to\Lambda$ be a ring section of $r$. Let $\theta:k\to\Lambda$ be additive, with $\theta(k)\subseteq I$, $\theta(1)=0$, and $\theta(ab)=i(a)\theta(b)+i(b)\theta(a)$, where $i:k\to\Lambda$ is the given structure map; derivations are as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Suppose $H_1(L_{K/k})$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] is finite dimensional over $K$. Then there exist an additive map $D:K\to\Lambda$ and a finite subset $f\subseteq I$ such that $D(1)=0$, $D(xy)=\sigma_0(x)D(y)+\sigma_0(y)D(x)$ for every $x,y\in K$, $D(K)\subseteq I$, and $\theta(a)-D(a)\in\operatorname{span}_k(f)$ for every $a\in k$, with the span formed using the given $k$-algebra structure on $\Lambda$.

proof.text: Equip I with its K-action by multiplication through the given section sigma0. The identity (ker r)I=0 makes any two lifts of the same residue scalar act equally, so compatibility identifies restriction to k with the given algebra action. The additive map theta with the stated Leibniz rule and theta(1)=0 is a derivation into I, and kills the prime field by additivity and the inverse product rule. Represent it by a k-linear map on the universal differentials over the prime field.

Choose a k-basis dy_j from the spanning exact differentials of k over the prime field and extend it to a K-basis of K tensor_k Omega_k. Apply the middle Jacobi--Zariski exactness statement (R,S,T)=(F_p,k,K): the kernel of the differential map is the image of the K-linear connecting map from H1Cotangent k K. This kernel is finite dimensional. Take a finite basis of it and the union J0 of the finite coordinate supports of its basis vectors. The kernel is contained in the span of dy_j with j in J0. Independence of the original basis shows that the images of dy_j for j outside J0 are independent in Omega_K.

Extend the independent differential images outside J0 to a K-basis of Omega_K. Define a K-linear map to I with the prescribed values theta(y_j) on those images and value zero on the additional basis vectors. Composing with the universal differential gives an additive map D with D(1)=0, the sigma0-Leibniz rule, and all its values in I. The k-linear map representing theta minus the restriction of D vanishes on dy_j outside J0. Therefore its value on da is a k-linear combination of the finitely many values at dy_j in J0. Let f be their finite image in Lambda. Every f_j lies in I; equality of the restricted residue action with the given k-action identifies this span with Submodule.span k f in Lambda.

theorem exists_finite_rank_defect_derivation
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (K : Type w) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (Λ : Type v) [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    (r : Λ →+* K) (hcomm : r.comp (algebraMap k Λ) = algebraMap k K)
    (I : Ideal Λ) (hI : I ≤ RingHom.ker r) (hkill : RingHom.ker r * I = ⊥)
    (σ0 : K →+* Λ) (hσ0 : r.comp σ0 = RingHom.id K)
    (theta : k →+ Λ) (htheta : ∀ a : k, theta a ∈ I)
    (htheta_one : theta 1 = 0)
    (htheta_mul : ∀ a b : k,
      theta (a * b) = algebraMap k Λ a * theta b + algebraMap k Λ b * theta a)
    (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)
    (hH : Module.Finite K (H1Cotangent k K)) :
    ∃ (D : K →+ Λ) (f : Finset Λ),
      D 1 = 0 ∧
      (∀ x y : K, D (x * y) = σ0 x * D y + σ0 y * D x) ∧
      (∀ x : K, D x ∈ I) ∧
      (f : Set Λ) ⊆ I ∧
      (∀ a : k, theta a - D (algebraMap k K a) ∈
        Submodule.span k (f : Set Λ))
